title: Container Bookings: rolls, overbooking order and carrier roll compensation
content:
## Policy clause
For the Container Bookings product line, a roll moves a booking off its allocated sailing to a later sailing of the same service. A carrier roll follows overbooking, a blank sailing or a port omission. When a sailing is overbooked, the line rolls bookings in descending order of loading priority rank, so the highest rank number is rolled first; a booking whose tier has guaranteed space is rolled only for a blank sailing or a port omission, never for overbooking.

Every roll is logged as one roll entry on the booking, carrying the sailing rolled off and who initiated it (carrier or customer), and the booking's vessel and voyage, ETD and three cut-offs are replaced by those of the new sailing.

**Compensation.** Compensation is credited only for a roll whose recorded initiator is carrier, as shown on that roll entry. The credit is reduced so that the roll compensation already credited on the booking before this credit, together with this credit, never exceeds the tier's compensation cap per booking. A tier whose compensation is 0.00 receives no credit and no entry is written. Each carrier roll is compensated at most once.

Carrier rolls never bear a fee, and they count toward the number of carrier rolls that opens free cancellation.

## Overbooking order (hypothetical ranks)
*Hypothetical sailing, for illustration only:* three bookings are on an overbooked sailing, with loading priority ranks 5 and 3 on tiers without guaranteed space, and a third on a tier with guaranteed space. The rank 5 booking is rolled before the rank 3 booking; the guaranteed-space booking is not rolled for the overbooking at all. Had the sailing been blanked instead, the guaranteed-space booking could be rolled as well.

## Points of judgement
**A customer asked to move to a later sailing. Is that roll compensated?** No. Only a roll recorded with the carrier as initiator earns compensation.

**The same carrier roll has already been compensated. May a second credit be written for it?** No. Each carrier roll is compensated at most once.

**What changes on the booking after a roll?** The sailing, the ETD and the cargo, SI and VGM cut-offs follow the new sailing; the roll entry keeps the sailing rolled off.

## Retired wording
The following two statements of this policy are **no longer in force** and have been superseded by the current basis for crediting carrier roll compensation:
- the former statement that the booking is credited the per-container compensation rate multiplied by its container count;
- the former statement that compensation is paid when the booking's count of carrier rolls, counted including the roll being compensated, does not exceed the tier's number of compensated carrier rolls.

superseded_clauses: the booking is credited roll_compensation_per_container_usd times its container_count
when booking_msr_carrier_rolls, counted including the roll being compensated, does not exceed max_compensated_carrier_rolls
